classification.difficultyReason: Infer the dimensions of identical rectangles from their arrangement, count shared fencing once, and use the resulting equation to calculate total area.

content.prompt: The rectangular paddock below is divided into eight identical rectangular paddocks. The total length of fencing used is 2100 metres. What is the total area?

spec.sourceRegion: Upper-left question 24, diagram beneath the stem.
spec.description: Landscape rectangle with eight identical rectangular regions: two upright rectangles on the upper left, three horizontal rectangles stacked centrally, one upright rectangle on the upper right, and two horizontal rectangles side by side along the bottom.
spec.mathematics: Each small rectangle has side ratio 1:3. The outer rectangle has proportional dimensions 6 by 4. Every outer and internal segment represents fencing, with shared segments counted once. Coordinate units establish proportions only and are not printed numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: No dimensions, labels or answers are shown.

inlines.text: Use the arrangement to find the side ratio, then count all fencing once.

answer.worked:
Let each small rectangle have width $x$ metres and length $y$ metres, with $y>x$. Comparing the total width along the top and bottom gives
$$\begin{align*}3x+y&=2y\\y&=3x.\end{align*}$$
Counting the outer boundary and each internal fence once gives a total fencing length of $6x+12y$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}6x+12y&=2100\\6x+12(3x)&=2100\\42x&=2100\\x&=50\\y&=3(50)\\y&=150.\end{align*}$$
The eight identical rectangles have total area
$$\begin{align*}A&=8xy\\A&=8(50)(150)\\A&=60\,000\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
